title: MTOGO — backend API requests and process
description: Slices #169/#170/#194/#171/#172/#173/#174/#175/#202/#182/#183: completed ordinary API responses, 5xx proportion, p95 latency and process CPU, memory and event-loop delay, with established streams and interrupted requests kept apart, from one HTTP-serving Medusa process, plus host CPU, load, memory, swap and free disk with the lowest memory and most swap over the displayed range, the Customer menu read by part and the storefront restaurant menu page render time, with explicit unavailable states. Per-view low- and high-traffic indications. No business counts.

list.name: Backend restarts
list.textFormat: A new HTTP-serving process started: usually a release or rollback, otherwise a crash. Process counters start again from 0.

list.name: low_traffic_threshold
list.label: Low traffic below (responses / 5 min, 0 = off)
list.description: Whole number 0–999999999999999. Changes only your view and its URL.

list.name: high_traffic_warning
list.label: High-traffic warning
list.description: Disabled by default. Enable to compare the count with High traffic above. Changes only your view and its URL.

list.name: high_traffic_threshold
list.label: High traffic above (responses / 5 min)
list.description: Whole number 0–999999999999999, validated always and compared only when the warning is enabled. Changes only your view and its URL.

options.content: **One HTTP-serving backend process** (`backend-metrics:9464`), completed ordinary API responses only: server-side HTTP latency, **not Order processing time**, not users or Orders (Feature #54). *Unavailable* means no current evidence, never zero. Coverage and limits: **How to read this dashboard** at the bottom.

panels.title: Browsing p95 within 2 s
panels.description: ADR-0014: 95 % of ordinary browsing and status requests within 2 s. The p95 of all ordinary API routes, the query of the Ordinary API p95 stat below; Order submission is in it too, so amber can be submission alone (see the slowest route patterns). Green below 2 s, amber from 2 s, red from 5 s. Unavailable without duration observations.

links.title: This requirement in the docs table

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(mtogo_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="mtogo-backend"}[5m]) and on(job, instance) (up{job="mtogo-backend"} == 1))) and on() (sum(increase(mtogo_http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="mtogo-backend"}[5m]) and on(job, instance) (up{job="mtogo-backend"} == 1)) > 0)

panels.title: Order submission p95 within 5 s
panels.description: ADR-0014: Order submission within 5 s with the mock payment provider answering at once. The p95 of POST /store/carts/:id/complete only, from the per-route p95 query (Latency by route over time). Green below 5 s, red from 5 s. Unavailable when no Order was submitted in the last five minutes.

panels.title: Server failures (5xx)
panels.description: Server failures as a share of completed responses, the query of the 5xx proportion stat below. Green at 0 %, amber above 0 %. Expected refusals (4xx) are not failures. Unavailable with no completed responses.

panels.title: Completed responses by status class — rolling 5 minutes
panels.description: Estimated completed ordinary API responses in the five minutes before each point, by status class, stacked. Per-series increase before aggregation, so a restart never shows negative traffic. 4xx includes expected refusals (bad key, signed out, not found); 5xx is a server failure. Gaps mean no current evidence. Exact statuses by route: Completed responses by final status.

panels.title: Completed responses by final status — since process start
panels.description: Final server-side status after response completion, counted once. Newly observed status series begin at their actual counter value. Gaps are not joined.

targets.expr: sum by (method, route, status) (mtogo_http_requests_total{job="mtogo-backend"} and on(job, instance) (up{job="mtogo-backend"} == 1))

panels.title: 5xx proportion — rolling 5 minutes
panels.description: Server-failure responses divided by all completed responses. A missing 5xx series counts as zero only when completed responses exist; zero traffic is unavailable, not 0%. A 5xx series appears on its first failure, so that first failure on a new route/status can still read 0% until the next one. Green at 0 %, amber above 0 %.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(mtogo_http_requests_total{job="mtogo-backend",status=~"5.."}[5m]) and on(job, instance) (up{job="mtogo-backend"} == 1)) or (0 * sum(rate(mtogo_http_requests_total{job="mtogo-backend"}[5m]) and on(job, instance) (up{job="mtogo-backend"} == 1)))) / (sum(rate(mtogo_http_requests_total{job="mtogo-backend"}[5m]) and on(job, instance) (up{job="mtogo-backend"} == 1)) > 0)

panels.title: Ordinary API p95 response time — rolling 5 minutes
panels.description: Estimated from aggregated histogram buckets (0.005–10 s). Unavailable without duration observations. A value of 10 s means at or above the top bucket. Green below 2 s (ADR-0014 browsing target), amber from 2 s, red from 5 s (Order submission target).

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(mtogo_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="mtogo-backend"}[5m]) and on(job, instance) (up{job="mtogo-backend"} == 1))) and on() (sum(increase(mtogo_http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="mtogo-backend"}[5m]) and on(job, instance) (up{job="mtogo-backend"} == 1)) > 0)

panels.title: Duration observations behind the p95 — rolling 5 minutes
panels.description: Estimated completed responses with a duration in the window. A p95 from a handful of observations is weak evidence.

panels.title: 5xx proportion — rolling 5 minutes
panels.description: Gaps mean zero completed responses or no current evidence, never 0%.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(mtogo_http_requests_total{job="mtogo-backend",status=~"5.."}[5m]) and on(job, instance) (up{job="mtogo-backend"} == 1)) or (0 * sum(rate(mtogo_http_requests_total{job="mtogo-backend"}[5m]) and on(job, instance) (up{job="mtogo-backend"} == 1)))) / (sum(rate(mtogo_http_requests_total{job="mtogo-backend"}[5m]) and on(job, instance) (up{job="mtogo-backend"} == 1)) > 0)

panels.title: Ordinary API p95 — all routes, rolling 5 minutes
panels.description: Gaps mean no duration observations or no current evidence. HTTP latency, not Order processing time.

panels.title: Slowest route patterns now — p95, rolling 5 minutes
panels.description: The ten route patterns with the highest p95 in the last five minutes, slowest first. Only routes with duration observations are listed; a p95 from a handful of requests is weak evidence (see the observation count). Green below 2 s, amber from 2 s, red from 5 s. History per route: the Latency by route over time row.

targets.expr: topk(10, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, method, route) (rate(mtogo_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="mtogo-backend"}[5m]) and on(job, instance) (up{job="mtogo-backend"} == 1))) and on(method, route) (sum by (method, route) (increase(mtogo_http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="mtogo-backend"}[5m]) and on(job, instance) (up{job="mtogo-backend"} == 1)) > 0))

panels.title: HTTP-serving process CPU — cores used, rolling 5 minutes
panels.description: rate(process_cpu_seconds_total[5m]): user plus system CPU seconds this one Node process used per second. 1 = one full core; it is not host utilization and has no 100% ceiling. Unavailable with fewer than two scrapes or no current evidence.

panels.title: HTTP-serving process memory — bytes
panels.description: Current resident memory (RSS): bytes the OS holds in RAM for this process, including code, V8 heap, buffers and native memory. The time series beside it also shows V8 heap used/total. The bar ends at 768 MiB, the staging backend container's memory cap; amber from 80 %, red from 90 %. The local demo has no cap.

panels.title: HTTP-serving process event-loop delay — seconds, per scrape window
panels.description: p99 over the window since the previous scrape. Collector-defined statistics of the time between ticks of Node's 10 ms event-loop sampling timer, in seconds, over the window since the previous Prometheus scrape (~15 s); every scrape resets them. A healthy process reads about 0.01 s, the sampling resolution itself; only time above that is delay. Sustained p99 above about 0.1 s means requests wait for the event loop. Green below 0.1 s, amber from 0.1 s, red from 1 s.

panels.title: HTTP-serving process CPU — cores used, rolling 5 minutes
panels.description: rate(process_cpu_seconds_total[5m]): user plus system CPU seconds this one Node process used per second. 1 = one full core; it is not host utilization and has no 100% ceiling. Unavailable with fewer than two scrapes or no current evidence.

panels.title: HTTP-serving process memory — bytes
panels.description: Resident memory (RSS, bytes the OS holds in RAM for this process) and V8 heap used/total (JavaScript objects). Resident is larger: it also covers code, buffers and native memory.

panels.title: HTTP-serving process event-loop delay — seconds, per scrape window
panels.description: Collector-defined statistics of the time between ticks of Node's 10 ms event-loop sampling timer, in seconds, over the window since the previous Prometheus scrape (~15 s); every scrape resets them. A healthy process reads about 0.01 s, the sampling resolution itself; only time above that is delay. Sustained p99 above about 0.1 s means requests wait for the event loop.

panels.title: Host CPU used — rolling 5 minutes
panels.description: Share of all cores' time spent working over five minutes: everything but idle and waiting for input or output, including time the hypervisor gave to other machines (steal). 100 % = every core busy. Whole host, unlike the HTTP-serving process CPU, which is in cores. No limit is agreed, so it has no colour. Unavailable with fewer than two scrapes or no current evidence.

targets.expr: sum by (job, instance) (rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{job="mtogo-node",mode!~"idle|iowait"}[5m])) / sum by (job, instance) (rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{job="mtogo-node"}[5m])) and on(job, instance) (up{job="mtogo-node"} == 1)

panels.title: Host load per core — 5 minutes
panels.description: Five-minute load average divided by the number of cores. Load counts tasks that run, wait for a core or wait for the disk. Around 1 means the cores are fully used; staying above 1 means work is queueing, and with a low CPU value the queue is at the disk. No limit is agreed, so it has no colour. Unavailable when Node Exporter is not being scraped.

targets.expr: node_load5{job="mtogo-node"} / on(job, instance) count by (job, instance) (node_cpu_seconds_total{job="mtogo-node",mode="idle"}) and on(job, instance) (up{job="mtogo-node"} == 1)

panels.title: Host memory available
panels.description: Memory the kernel can still hand out without swapping (`available` in `free -m`), of the whole host: the applications, monitoring and everything else on it. Red below 200 MB (200 MiB), the agreed floor: roll back the monitoring stack (staging runbook). Unavailable when Node Exporter is not being scraped.

panels.title: Host memory available — lowest in the displayed range
panels.description: The lowest memory available (`available` in `free -m`) of the whole host in the displayed range, as one number for the staging capacity table. Red below 200 MB (200 MiB), the agreed floor. The window is the displayed time range (`$__range`), not five minutes: this stat and its swap partner are the agreed exception to the five-minute rule, so zooming to one deploy, between its restart markers, gives that deploy's reading. Every 15-second scrape in the range counts; scrapes while Node Exporter was down do not. Unavailable when Node Exporter was not scraped at any point in the range, never a stale or zero value.

panels.title: Host swap used
panels.description: Swap in use on the whole host. No limit is agreed, so it has no colour. Read it next to memory available: swap that keeps growing while memory is low means the host is too small. 0 B is also shown by a host without swap. Unavailable when Node Exporter is not being scraped.

panels.title: Host swap used — most in the displayed range
panels.description: The most swap in use on the whole host in the displayed range, as one number for the staging capacity table. No limit is agreed, so it has no colour; read it next to the lowest memory available. 0 B is also shown by a host without swap. The window is the displayed time range (`$__range`), not five minutes: this stat and the lowest memory available are the agreed exception to the five-minute rule, so zooming to one deploy, between its restart markers, gives that deploy's reading. Every 15-second scrape in the range counts; scrapes while Node Exporter was down do not. Unavailable when Node Exporter was not scraped at any point in the range, never a stale or zero value.

panels.title: Host disk free — root file system
panels.description: Space an ordinary process can still use on the host's root file system, as a share of its size (`Avail` in `df`). Amber below 20 %, red below 10 %. The database, images, logs, Loki and Prometheus can share this disk, so a low value is not always monitoring. Unavailable when Node Exporter is not being scraped or cannot read the disk.

panels.title: Host disk free — Docker volumes
panels.description: Space an ordinary process can still use on the disk that holds the Docker volumes, as a share of its size (`Avail` in `df`). On the Droplet it is the same disk as the root file system. Amber below 20 %, red below 10 %. The database, images, logs, Loki and Prometheus can share this disk, so a low value is not always monitoring. Unavailable when Node Exporter is not being scraped or cannot read the disk.

panels.title: Host memory available
panels.description: Memory the kernel can still hand out without swapping (`available` in `free -m`), of the whole host: the applications, monitoring and everything else on it. Red below 200 MB (200 MiB), the agreed floor: roll back the monitoring stack (staging runbook). Unavailable when Node Exporter is not being scraped. The dashed line is the floor; gaps mean no current evidence.

panels.title: Host swap used
panels.description: Swap in use on the whole host. No limit is agreed, so it has no colour. Read it next to memory available: swap that keeps growing while memory is low means the host is too small. 0 B is also shown by a host without swap. Unavailable when Node Exporter is not being scraped.

panels.title: Host disk free
panels.description: Free share of both disks. Dashed lines: amber below 20 %, red below 10 %. On the Droplet the two are the same disk, so the lines cover each other. Gaps mean no current evidence.

panels.title: Host CPU used — rolling 5 minutes
panels.description: Share of all cores' time spent working over five minutes: everything but idle and waiting for input or output, including time the hypervisor gave to other machines (steal). 100 % = every core busy. Whole host, unlike the HTTP-serving process CPU, which is in cores. No limit is agreed, so it has no colour. Unavailable with fewer than two scrapes or no current evidence.

targets.expr: sum by (job, instance) (rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{job="mtogo-node",mode!~"idle|iowait"}[5m])) / sum by (job, instance) (rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{job="mtogo-node"}[5m])) and on(job, instance) (up{job="mtogo-node"} == 1)

panels.title: Host load average and cores
panels.description: Load over 1, 5 and 15 minutes next to the number of cores. Load counts tasks that run, wait for a core or wait for the disk; staying above the cores line means work is queueing. Gaps mean no current evidence.

targets.expr: count by (job, instance) (node_cpu_seconds_total{job="mtogo-node",mode="idle"}) and on(job, instance) (up{job="mtogo-node"} == 1)

options.content: **Kept apart from ordinary API panels.** An established server-sent event (SSE) stream, currently the partner kitchen feed `/partner/orders/stream`, is open for minutes or hours, so it is **not in the completed response** counts, rates or p95 above. It shows as one active connection while open and one termination when it ends: `server_ended` (the server closed it: session expiry, revoked access or a feed error; a deploy stops collection first, so feeds it ends are not recorded) or `disconnected` (the connection closed first). A disconnect is **not an application error** or a business failure; browsers reconnect. A **refused stream** (for example 401) never opened, so it stays an ordinary completed response. An **interrupted request** is an ordinary request whose connection closed before its response completed. It has **no HTTP status** and no duration, and a late failure after the disconnect adds no 500. A route of `unrouted` means no route had matched yet. Same target and five-minute window as the panels above; Unavailable means no current scrape.

panels.title: Server-sent event connections — active now
panels.description: Established streams open at the last scrape. 0 with a current scrape means none are open.

panels.title: Server-sent event terminations — rolling 5 minutes
panels.description: Estimated established streams that ended in the window, by any outcome. Needs two scrapes.

panels.title: Interrupted requests — rolling 5 minutes
panels.description: Estimated ordinary requests closed before a completed response in the window. Needs two scrapes.

panels.title: Server-sent event connections — active now
panels.description: Open established streams per stream route at each scrape. Gaps remain visible.

panels.title: Server-sent event terminations — rolling 5 minutes
panels.description: Per-series increase before aggregation; resets do not produce negative values. Gaps remain visible.

targets.expr: sum by (route, outcome) (increase(mtogo_sse_connections_closed_total{job="mtogo-backend"}[5m]) and on(job, instance) (up{job="mtogo-backend"} == 1))

panels.description: Per-series increase before aggregation, by bounded method and matched route pattern. Gaps remain visible.

targets.expr: sum by (method, route) (increase(mtogo_http_requests_interrupted_total{job="mtogo-backend"}[5m]) and on(job, instance) (up{job="mtogo-backend"} == 1))

panels.title: Customer menu read and restaurant menu page (#202)
Customer menu read and restaurant menu page

options.content: **What a Customer waits for on a Restaurant's menu** (#202). The backend route `GET /store/restaurants/:id/menu` comes from the request histogram above. Its parts come from the same backend target: `restaurant` (Restaurant, categories and dish ids), `dish_prices` (dishes with Medusa's calculated DKK prices), `photos` (dish photo records and the cover URL), `photo_urls` (signing the published dishes' photo URLs) and `food_information` (allergen and food-label catalogue, kept in memory between reads), plus `whole_read`, which counts only reads that answer with a menu. `dish_prices` and `photos` run at the same time, so the parts do not add up to the whole read. A read over 1 s also writes one `menu.read.slow` log line with each part in milliseconds. The page panels come from a **second private exporter, the staging `storefront` container**, target `storefront-metrics:9465` (job `mtogo-storefront`): server-side render time of `/[countryCode]/restaurants/[id]` from request start to the last byte, by kind: `document` (full page load), `navigation` (client-side navigation), `prefetch` (link prefetch) and `action` (a basket change answered with a fresh render of the page). Redirects (3xx) and renders whose connection closed first are not counted. No Restaurant ids, URLs or query strings are labels. In the local demo there is no storefront, so its target is DOWN and the page panels stay empty.

panels.title: Customer menu reads over 1 s — rolling 5 minutes
panels.description: Share of completed menu reads that took over one second on the backend. The issue #202 target is below 5%. Unavailable without menu reads in the window.

targets.expr: 1 - (sum(rate(mtogo_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="mtogo-backend",method="GET",route="/store/restaurants/:id/menu",le="1"}[5m]) and on(job, instance) (up{job="mtogo-backend"} == 1)) / (sum(rate(mtogo_http_request_duration_seconds_count{job="mtogo-backend",method="GET",route="/store/restaurants/:id/menu"}[5m]) and on(job, instance) (up{job="mtogo-backend"} == 1)) > 0))

panels.description: 1 = scrape succeeded; 0 = scrape failed; no data = no target observations. The local demo has no storefront, so it shows DOWN there.

options.content: **One HTTP-serving backend process**, target `backend-metrics:9464`: the local demo, or the staging `backend` container with browser and server-side calls from the storefront and partner app (a split staging worker serves no HTTP). Every completed ordinary API response, by matched route pattern. Method-less middleware finishing before any route matches gives fixed categories: refusals (publishable key, namespace or method-less authentication, malformed body) as `early_rejection`, 404s as `unmatched`, successes such as CORS preflights as `unrouted`; unknown methods as `OTHER`. A wildcard middleware refusal shows its wildcard. IDs/query strings never become labels. Health, `/app` Admin assets, `/static`, scrapes and established SSE streams are excluded, and so are interrupted requests; both have their own panels below.

**HTTP responses, not Customers or Orders.** Latency is server-side seconds from request start to response finish for one HTTP request. It is **not Order processing time** (Feature #54) or any business measure. Every query uses a rolling five-minute window; counts are extrapolated estimates. **Unavailable** means no valid evidence: target DOWN or absent, fewer than two scrapes, zero completed responses (no 5xx proportion) or no duration observations (no p95). Check the observation count before trusting a p95; p95 is capped at the 10 s bucket. Rates handle counter resets. Established streams and interrupted requests are separate and never enter these counts, rates or p95.

Both compare the controls at the top with **Estimated completed responses** (rolling five minutes, same estimate and exclusions), whatever range is displayed. **Low traffic below:** a count strictly below it is **LOW**; equal is not; **0 turns it off.** **High-traffic warning:** **Disabled** by default; when **Enabled**, a count strictly above **High traffic above** is **HIGH**; equal is not, and an enabled `0` is a real threshold, unlike Disabled. Thresholds allow digits only, `0` to `999999999999999`, no sign, decimal, exponent, spaces or leading zeros. An invalid value, or Low traffic below above an enabled High traffic above, shows a **configuration error** on both panels, never a fallback; High traffic above is validated even while Disabled, but only compared with Low traffic below when Enabled. Equal bounds are valid. Your values change this view and its URL (share the URL to share the settings), not the Git defaults or anyone else's view. No setting turns DOWN or missing data into a count, and HIGH is not a request limit, capacity claim or notification.

**One HTTP-serving backend Node process**, the same target `backend-metrics:9464` (job `mtogo-backend`) as the request panels: the local demo backend, or the staging `backend` container. Values come from the Prometheus client's standard process collectors on each scrape. **CPU** is cores used by this process (1 = one full CPU core), **not host utilization**: the Droplet has other processes and cores. **Memory** is bytes: resident set and V8 heap. **Event-loop delay** is seconds between 10 ms sampling ticks, over the window since the previous scrape; about 0.01 s is the healthy floor. Not covered: a separate worker process, the Next.js storefront and partner apps, the host or container, PostgreSQL and Redis. CPU seconds count from exporter start; a restart resets them and rates handle it.

**The host this monitoring stack runs on**, read by Node Exporter (`node-exporter:9100`, job `mtogo-node`) every 15 seconds: on staging the Droplet, locally the Docker engine's host, which with Docker Desktop is its virtual machine and not your computer. **CPU, load, memory, swap and disk are the whole host's, not per container**: MTOGO, the monitoring stack and everything else on it; for one container use `docker stats`. The memory floor of 200 MB is `available` in `free -m`. **Root file system** and **Docker volumes** are the same disk on the Droplet, so both read the same there. A short dip between two scrapes is not seen. **CPU used** is a share of all cores, unlike the process CPU, which is in cores; **load per core** counts tasks that run or wait, for a core or for the disk.
